newsitem.title: USA: Judge declares mistrial in Orange County trial.
newsitem.headline: Judge declares mistrial in Orange County trial.

text.p: The first criminal trial arising from the unprecedented bankruptcy of California's Orange County ended in a mistrial on Friday after the jury was unable to reach a verdict.

Superior Court Judge J. Stephen Czuleger declared a mistrial in the case of former Orange County Budget Director Ronald Rubino. Afterwards, a clerk for the court said jury selection for a new trial was set to begin on October 8.
Rubino, 44, was indicted by a county grand jury in December 1995 for allegedly aiding former county Treasurer Robert Citron in diverting funds from other government agencies for the county's benefit.
His trial began in early August.
Prosecutors portrayed an ambitious county employee who helped to steal millions of dollars away from unsuspecting cities, schools and special districts.
The defense asserted Rubino was unaware of the alleged diversion scheme.
The 11-woman, one man jury began its deliberations in Santa Ana on September 4.
Earlier this week, jurors told the judge they believed they were deadlocked, but they continued deliberations Thursday.
Friday morning, jurors told Czuleger they were hopelessly deadlocked. The foreman of the panel said jurors were split 9-to-3 in favor of acquittal.
Czuleger asked each juror if there was anything more the court could do to assist them in reaching a verdict and if they felt more time deliberating would help.
"With the conditions right now, we'll go crazy in that room," the sole male juror said.

Several jurors said there was confusion among the panel on how to apply the law in this case. One juror said it would be impossible for this jury to reach a verdict "unless you broke the law down in simple layman terms."
Another juror said a verdict could not be reached because "too much ignorance abounds" on the panel.
Orange County District Attorney Michael Capizzi said his office would immediately begin to prepare for the new trial.
"This will give us an opportunity to evaluate the defense evidence and do the things that are necessary to make it a stronger case next time," Capizzi said.
Defense attorneys were not immediately available to comment.

Rubino, who has denied any wrongdoing, was indicted on felony counts of misappropriating public funds and failing to transfer public funds. The counts covered his conduct in 1993 and 1994 when he worked in the county administrative office.
The maximum punishment for the charges was nine years in state prison.
Rubino's criminal trial was the first arising from the Orange County bankruptcy, the largest municipal bankruptcy in U.S. history.
Orange County filed for protection under Chapter 9 of the federal Bankruptcy Code on Dec. 6, 1994, after sustaining investment losses of more than $1.6 billion.
The county emerged from bankruptcy in June of this year.
